Mia (Sales): @Raghav heads-up — Zenith POC hitting truncated SSE chunks in their web demo using our wasm-sdk. Stream appears then stops; client throws 'Unexpected end of input' while parsing partial JSON.

Raghav (SE): Can you paste a raw snippet of the SSE stream and the client error stack? Also what SDK version are they on?

Mia (Sales): Logs from customer (redacted):
```
:event: completion
data: {"id":"abc123","tokens":"Hello"

:event: completion
data: {"id":"abc123","tokens":" wor"
```
Client console: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` in wasm-sdk stream parser. They say this happens ~20-40% of requests, more on chrome on slower mobile networks. SDK reported is `@redwood/wasm-sdk@1.3.5`

Devon (Eng): Likely causes: proxy/nginx buffering (flush boundaries), Transfer-Encoding headers not preserved, or our wasm incremental UTF-8 decoder not handling truncated multibyte sequences. Two quick checks: 1) confirm server sends `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and 2) try `curl -N` to observe live chunk boundaries.

Olivia (Client Eng): I saw identical behavior in an in-house repro with a reverse proxy that enabled gzip + buffer. The browser receives multiple `message` events where each event contains only a fragment of the JSON body. Their EventSource handler naively calls `JSON.parse(event.data)` which fails on partial fragments.

Raghav (SE): If they can't change the proxy immediately, there's a small client work-around: buffer consecutive EventSource messages keyed by id until you have a full JSON. Example pseudo: 
```
const buffer = {};
es.addEventListener('message', e => {
  const partial = e.data;
  const meta = tryParsePartialMeta(partial); // pull out id/seq
  buffer[meta.id] = (buffer[meta.id] || '') + meta.payload;
  try { const obj = JSON.parse(buffer[meta.id]); handle(obj); delete buffer[meta.id]; }
  catch (err) { /* keep buffering */ }
});
```
This is cheap for POC/demo.

Devon (Eng): Also, we pushed a fix for incremental UTF-8 handling in `wasm-sdk@1.3.7` — the decoder now preserves incomplete multi-byte sequences between chunks instead of failing. Recommend upgrade if they use our built-in parser. If they can't upgrade, the buffering workaround above prevents JSON.parse crashes.

Mia (Sales): Good call. Can we confirm whether this is a blocker for the demo next week? They said they hit it during a live walkthrough.

Olivia (Client Eng): For demo: enable websocket fallback in the SDK config — websockets give you cleaner framing (one message per frame). That avoids SSE chunk boundary ambiguity. For production, prefer addressing proxy flush settings or remove response compression for streaming endpoints.

Devon (Eng): Quick troubleshooting checklist for them to run (send back to Zenith):
- curl -N --compressed https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/<id> and paste raw output
- check proxy/nginx `proxy_buffering off;` and `gzip off;` for the streaming route
- capture HAR from Chrome (Preserve log) and share the first failing request
- try `@redwood/wasm-sdk@1.3.7` to see if it reduces failures

Mia (Sales): I'll relay checklist. Also customer asked about pricing/timeline — if they must switch to websocket fallback for the demo, any config complexity or cost impact?

Raghav (SE): No cost impact. Websocket fallback just changes client transport; on our side it routes to same model worker. For Dedicated customers we can open websocket ports in config; for Hosted it's already supported. Should be trivial to flip for a demo.

sre-bot: Deployment to prod/streaming-fixes v2026.03.19 completed by @devon — release includes wasm-sdk 1.3.7 and a streaming decoder fix.

Devon (Eng): Action items: 1) Mia: get HAR + curl output from Zenith, 2) Olivia: send sample buffering snippet to them + websocket fallback hint, 3) Raghav: follow up on SDK upgrade test, 4) I'll monitor errors next 48h and rollback if any regression.

Mia (Sales): Sending checklist now. I'll ask them to try the client buffer hack first (fastest) and/or switch to ws fallback for the walkthrough. Will confirm once they try. Thanks team :pray:
